https://www.myjoyonline.com/us-exchange-.body: A 2019 Mandela Washington Fellow, Dr Joel Afi Duah, says it is becoming increasingly difficult for beneficiaries of development programs in the United States of America to access post-fellowship grants following donor cuts in the US. Dr. Duah, who is the municipal director of Health Services for Tano South in the Ahafo Region, says the situation has limited alumni efforts to translate knowledge and skills acquired through exchange programmes into practical development projects. He was speaking at the U.S. Embassy Ghana Exchange Alumni Summit in Kumasi. “With the cuts in funding, alumni are leveraging their networks and available resources to sustain their work. However, it has become quite difficult to plan and execute capital projects and meet other major expenses,” he said. He called on the government to increase funding for public institutions struggling with reductions and withdrawals in support from international development partners. He says funding cuts by organisations, including the United States Agency for International Development (USAID) and the United States African Development Foundation (USADF), have disrupted development programmes and weakened the capacity of institutions and beneficiaries to sustain ongoing initiatives. “We are therefore making a passionate appeal to the government to step up funding support in areas where donor funding has been reduced or withdrawn. This will enable us to build on the investments made and the knowledge and skills we have acquired through these fellowship programmes,” he asserted. Dr Duah believes increased government investment will be critical to sustaining the gains made through international partnerships and ensuring that development initiatives do not stall because of funding constraints. The appeal comes as the U.S. Embassy in Ghana brings together about 100 alumni of U.S. government exchange programmes from the Ashanti Region and Ghana’s middle belt for an Alumni Excellence Summit in Kumasi. The event, held on Saturday, November 21, 2026, celebrated the contributions of former exchange programme participants to national development across various sectors. It also forms part of activities marking the 250th anniversary of American independence under the Freedom 250 initiative. Cultural Affairs Attaché at the U.S. Embassy in Ghana, Donya Eldridge, said the exchange programmes are intended to promote knowledge-sharing and expose participants to approaches the US has adopted in addressing development challenges that Ghana also faces. “Our alumni include students and professionals who have had the opportunity to learn from experiences in the United States. The idea is to share what they have done, the lessons they have learned, and help us understand how similar approaches can work in the Ghanaian economy,” she stated
https://www.myjoyonline.com/us-exchange-.title_zh: 美国交换生峰会：以往奖学金获得者难以获得结业后的资助，限制了知识转移申请
https://www.myjoyonline.com/us-exchange-.body_zh: 2019年曼德拉·华盛顿研究员乔尔·阿菲·杜阿博士表示，随着美国捐助方削减资金，美国发展规划受益者在研究员访学结束后获得后续资助正变得越来越困难。杜阿博士是阿哈福地区塔诺南市卫生服务处主任。他说，处境困难限制了校友将交流项目中学到的知识和技能转化为实际发展项目。他在库马西举行的美国驻加纳使馆交流项目校友峰会上说：“随着资金削减，校友们正利用自己的人脉和现有资源维持工作。然而，规划和执行资本项目以及支付其他大额开支已变得相当困难。”他呼吁政府增加对公共机构的资助；这些机构正因国际发展伙伴削减或撤回支持而举步维艰。他说，包括美国国际开发署（USAID）和美国非洲发展基金会（USADF）在内的组织削减资金，已扰乱发展规划项目，并削弱了机构和受益者维持现有工作的能力。他断言：“因此，我们强烈呼吁政府增加对捐助资金已被削减或撤回领域的资金支持。这将使我们能够巩固已作出的投入，并利用我们通过这些研究员项目获得的知识和技能。”杜阿博士认为，增加政府投资对于维持国际伙伴关系带来的成果，以及确保发展规划项目不因资金受限而停滞至关重要。在美国驻加纳使馆于库马西举办杰出校友峰会、汇集约100名来自阿散蒂地区及加纳中部地带美国政府交流项目校友之际，这项呼吁也随之发出。活动于2026年11月21日星期六举行，旨在表彰前交流项目参与者对各领域国家发展所作的贡献。这也是“自由250”倡议下庆祝美国独立250周年系列活动的一部分。美国驻加纳使馆文化事务随员唐娅·埃尔德里奇说，这些交流项目旨在促进知识分享，让参与者了解美国在应对加纳同样面临的发展挑战时采用的方法。她表示：“我们的校友包括曾有机会向美国学习的学生和专业人士。我们的理念是分享他们的实践、他们吸取的经验，并帮助我们了解类似做法如何适用于加纳经济。”

https://www.koreatimes.co.kr/southkorea/.body: Unification Minister nominee Hong Ihk-pyo is a three-term lawmaker and a close political ally of President Lee Jae Myung with North Korea expertise. Born in 1967, he studied political science at Hanyang University. Before entering politics, he worked as a researcher at the Korea Institute for International Economic Policy and as a policy adviser to the Ministry of Unification. He also taught as a professor at the University of North Korean Studies. He won election to the National Assembly three times, serving from 2012 to 2024. Hong served as floor leader of the ruling Democratic Party of Korea from September 2023 to May 2024 when Lee was party chair. Earlier this year, Hong was appointed as senior presidential secretary for political affairs, handling coordination with the National Assembly and the political parties. If confirmed, he will succeed Chung Dong-young, who has served as unification minister since July last year

https://www.koreatimes.co.kr/southkorea/.body: Foreign Minister nominee Lim Woong-soon, currently a senior presidential security official, is a former veteran diplomat well versed in relations with the United States and diplomacy with North Korea. Since President Lee Jae Myung took office in June last year, Lim has served as the second deputy director of the National Security Office at Cheong Wa Dae, assisting the president in making key foreign policy and security decisions. His nomination came as South Korea's chief diplomat faces a host of foreign policy tasks, ranging from implementing security, trade and investment agreements with the U.S. to handling North Korea-related diplomacy and ensuring cooperation with China, Japan and other countries. Since entering foreign service in 1988, Lim has served in various posts at home and abroad, including as ambassador to Canada, deputy consul general in New York, minister for political affairs at the embassy in Washington, and other posts in Austria, Italy, France and Spain. Presidential chief of staff Lim Kwang-hyun portrayed Lim as being well suited to maximize the achievements of "practical diplomacy centering on national interests" — a term referring to the president's foreign policy mantra — by strengthening cooperation with the U.S and expanding South Korea's overall diplomatic horizons. The nominee was born in the central city of Daejeon in 1964. He graduated from Yonsei University's economics department

Song Seog-jun of the main opposition People Power Party said during an interview with The Korea Times, Wednesday, noting that South Korea still relies heavily on military intelligence from both the U.S. and Japan.
https://www.koreatimes.co.kr/foreignaffa.summary_zh: 主要反对党国民力量党议员宋锡俊周三接受《韩国时报》采访时表示：“韩国目前在与美国的情报合作方面存在不协调，如果不迅速恢复合作，可能升级为严重的安全危机。”他指出，韩国目前仍高度依赖美国和日本提供的军事情报。
https://www.koreatimes.co.kr/foreignaffa.body: “Korea is currently experiencing dissonance with the U.S. in intelligence cooperation, which could escalate into a grave security crisis if not restored quickly,” Rep. Song Seog-jun of the main opposition People Power Party said during an interview with The Korea Times, Wednesday, noting that South Korea still relies heavily on military intelligence from both the U.S. and Japan. “We must solidify ties with our traditional allies so that South Korea can effectively leverage the mature and robust national strength it has built,” he said, adding that stronger alliances could compel North Korea, China and Russia to offer concessions. His remarks came amid lingering friction in Seoul-Washington security and trade ties, ranging from delays in investment negotiations to restrictions on intelligence sharing about North Korea, even as ties among Pyongyang, Beijing and Moscow continue to deepen. Song argued that South Korea’s international standing is stronger than ever and that it is time for Seoul to act accordingly. “During the period when we had lost our national sovereignty, we had no choice but to simply go along with the decisions of major powers, but things are different now,” the lawmaker said. "Our manufacturing capabilities have grown across the board, from advanced semiconductors to defense production and our shipbuilding technology is world-class. All of this reflects how much stronger we’ve become as a country and how much better equipped we are to respond in a crisis." Referencing Seo Hui, a 10th-century civil official who secured territorial concessions from the Khitan empire through negotiation rather than battle, Song said South Korea has a distinctive capacity for cooperation and must channel it into proactive diplomatic leadership. “South Korea has a distinctive capacity for conciliation — what I call a spirit of mutual prosperity and harmony. Now is the time to channel that strength into proactive, assertive diplomatic leadership, taking the initiative to mediate competing national interests and guide this complex landscape toward a positive outcome,” he said. He criticized the Lee Jae Myung administration for imposing excessive regulations on businesses, which could undermine diplomatic potential. “These excessive corporate regulations could weaken companies and ultimately undermine South Korea’s national strength and long-term prospects,” Song said. “South Korea–China economic ties used to be remarkably strong. As the saying ‘security with the U.S., economy with China’ suggests, China served as our largest export market and a mutually complementary trading partner,” he said. Asked how to improve inter-Korean relations, Song urged patience and consistency. “It may sound overly idealistic at a moment like this, but we must stay true to fundamentals — engaging North Korea consistently, patiently and unwaveringly while offering a shared vision for the future,” he said, adding the two Koreas have long-standing principles of mutual non-aggression, exchange and trust-building. He said advances in digital technology now offer new ways to reach the North Korean public directly. “While outreach to the North once relied mainly on loudspeaker broadcasts and leaflets, advancing digital technologies and modern communications will increasingly allow us to share information about a better future and I believe the North Korean people will awaken,” he said, adding that North Korea cannot remain isolated indefinitely
https://www.koreatimes.co.kr/foreignaffa.title_zh: 议员警告，与美国的情报分歧若不能迅速解决，可能演变成安全危机
https://www.koreatimes.co.kr/foreignaffa.body_zh: “韩国目前在情报合作问题上与美国出现不协调，如果不能迅速恢复合作，可能升级为严重的安全危机。”国民力量党主要反对派议员宋石俊周三接受《韩国时报》采访时表示，韩国目前仍高度依赖美国和日本提供的军事情报。他说：“我们必须与传统盟友巩固关系，使韩国能够有效运用自己打造的成熟而强大的国家实力。”他还说，更紧密的联盟关系可能迫使朝鲜、中国和俄罗斯作出让步。此番言论出台之际，首尔与华盛顿之间的安全和贸易关系仍存在摩擦，问题从投资谈判延迟到限制有关朝鲜的情报共享；与此同时，平壤、北京和莫斯科之间的关系持续深化。宋认为，韩国当下的国际地位比以往任何时候都更强，首尔是时候采取相应行动。这位议员说：“在失去国家主权的时期，我们别无选择，只能顺从大国的决定，但现在情况不同了。我们的制造业能力已全面提升，从先进半导体到国防生产，我们的造船技术也位居世界前列。这一切都反映了我们作为一个国家变得多么强大，以及我们应对危机的能力得到了多大提升。”宋提到10世纪时通过谈判而非战争从契丹帝国取得领土让步的官员徐晦，称韩国具备独特的合作能力，必须将其转化为积极主动的外交领导力。他说：“韩国拥有独特的调和能力——我称之为共同繁荣与和谐精神。现在是时候把这种力量转化为积极主动、敢于作为的外交领导，主动调解彼此冲突的国家利益，并引导这一复杂局势走向积极结果。”他批评李在明政府对企业施加过度监管，因为这可能削弱外交潜力。宋说：“这些过度的企业监管会削弱企业竞争力，最终损害韩国的国家实力和长期前景。”他说：“过去，韩国与中国的经济关系极为紧密。正如‘安全靠美国、经济靠中国’这一说法所表明的，中国曾是我们的最大出口市场和互利互补的贸易伙伴。”当被问及如何改善韩朝关系时，宋敦促保持耐心和一贯性。他说：“在这样的时刻，这听起来或许过于理想主义，但我们必须坚守根本——始终如一、耐心且坚定不移地与朝鲜接触，同时向其提出共同的未来愿景。”他还说，朝韩双方长期以来一直奉行互不侵犯、交流和建立信任等原则。他表示，数字技术的进步如今提供了直接接触朝鲜民众的新途径。他说：“过去，对北方的宣传主要依靠扩音器广播和传单，而数字技术和现代通信的进步将让我们越来越能够分享美好未来的信息。我相信，朝鲜人民会觉醒。”他还说，朝鲜不可能永远处于孤立状态……

https://www.koreatimes.co.kr/lifestyle/p.body: Felix of K-pop group Stray Kids is putting a modern face on traditional Korean clothing, called "hanbok," joining five local designers in a fashion campaign set to reach audiences in six major cities around the world. The Ministry of Culture, Sports and Tourism said Monday it had unveiled the 2026 Hanbok Wave campaign, featuring the internationally popular singer in a series of photographs showcasing contemporary interpretations of traditional Korean dress. The project, organized with the Korea Craft and Design Foundation, pairs promising domestic hanbok brands with prominent figures from Korean popular culture to reinterpret traditional clothing for modern audiences and promote it internationally. Their designs draw on traditional Korean aesthetics while introducing contemporary silhouettes, materials and decorative techniques. The collection includes layered garments inspired by traditional robes, coats featuring landscapes drawn from Korean ink paintings and designs incorporating mother-of-pearl patterns. Other pieces reinterpret the eight trigrams used in East Asian divination practices and combine traditional military-style robes with intricate embroidery. The ministry said the collaboration with Felix offers an opportunity to present hanbok's distinctive beauty and cultural significance to a global audience while demonstrating its potential as contemporary fashion. Starting in the first week of December, campaign images will appear on major digital billboards in Seoul, including a panoramic display at Seoul Station, and in New York, Paris, Milan, Tokyo, Jakarta and Rio de Janeiro. Jakarta and Rio de Janeiro are new additions to this year's campaign. Photographs and videos will also be released through the ministry's and foundation's official social media channels, while Marie Claire Korea will publish a feature on Felix and the five designers. "The ministry will continue to support hanbok as contemporary cultural content that connects with people around the world and help Korean hanbok brands expand into international markets," Myung said. https://www.koreatimes.co.kr/economy/oth.title: Korea ready to deploy market stabilization fund if conditions warrant: finance minister
https://www.koreatimes.co.kr/economy/oth.summary: Korea will decide whether to deploy its stock market stabilization fund based on how market conditions evolve, Minister of Finance and Economy Lee Hyoung-il said Monday, a day after the government began preparations. “We are reviewing the steps needed in case market conditions warrant activating the fund,” Lee said at a press conference.
https://www.koreatimes.co.kr/economy/oth.summary_zh: 财政经济部长李亨il周一表示，韩国将根据市场状况的发展，决定是否动用股市稳定基金；就在政府启动相关准备工作的第二天。他说：“我们正在审查在市场状况需要启动该基金时所需采取的措施。”李亨il在新闻发布会上说。
https://www.koreatimes.co.kr/economy/oth.body: Korea will decide whether to deploy its stock market stabilization fund based on how market conditions evolve, Minister of Finance and Economy Lee Hyoung-il said Monday, a day after the government began preparations. Lee said the government would continue to monitor the market before deciding on the timing and size of any deployment. “We are reviewing the steps needed in case market conditions warrant activating the fund,” Lee said at a press conference. “We will decide on the details as we assess how the situation evolves.” Lee said the review was intended to ensure the fund could be deployed smoothly if needed, given how long it had been idle. Asked whether the government would expand the fund, he said authorities would assess market conditions at the time of any deployment before deciding on its size. His remarks came as growing doubts about the outlook for artificial intelligence (AI) and returns on AI investment dented investor confidence. The tech-heavy Nasdaq fell and Korean shares dropped sharply as volatility increased across global markets. At an emergency meeting Sunday, Lee and the heads of the Bank of Korea, the Financial Services Commission and the Financial Supervisory Service (FSS) agreed to prepare for possible deployment of the market stabilization fund and review how it would operate in practice. The FSS and the Korea Exchange also announced a three-month period of intensified monitoring for illegal short selling. The fund pools money from brokerages, banks and other institutions to buy shares when demand dries up during steep market declines. Authorities last used a market stabilization fund to intervene in 2008, during the global financial crisis, deploying 515 billion won ($382 million). A separate fund worth 10.76 trillion won was established in 2020 during the COVID-19 pandemic and has remained unused. Lee vowed to keep a close watch on trading because the market’s direction was difficult to predict. When asked about further measures, Lee said, “We already have contingency plans in place. We are preparing to take action at the appropriate time.” He said authorities would use the three-month period to step up enforcement against illegal short selling and monitor for unfair trading. Lee expects AI investment to continue rising in the near term despite concerns about financing and regulation. He said Korea’s two major chipmakers, Samsung Electronics and SK hynix, had secured substantial orders under long-term supply contracts and that their memory chip inventories were falling rapidly. He also expects potential regulatory changes following the U.S. midterm elections to have a limited impact on AI data center construction next year, as most U.S. projects slated to begin construction have already secured permits. Lee, meanwhile, said Korea’s economy was likely to grow in the high 3 percent range this year, barring an unexpected shock. Asked about forecasts from some investment banks for growth of 4 percent or more, he said, “Mathematically, I think 4 percent is within reach,” adding that the outcome would depend on fourth-quarter growth
https://www.koreatimes.co.kr/economy/oth.title_zh: 韩国财政部长：条件符合时，韩国准备部署市场稳定基金
https://www.koreatimes.co.kr/economy/oth.body_zh: 韩国财政经济部长李炯一（Lee Hyoung-il）周一表示，政府将根据市场状况的演变，决定是否动用股市稳定基金；就在前一天，政府已启动相关准备工作。李说，在决定任何注资的时机和规模之前，政府将继续监测市场。他在一场新闻发布会上说：“我们正在审查市场状况需要时启动基金所需的步骤。随着我们评估局势如何发展，我们将决定具体安排。”李说，鉴于该基金已闲置较长时间，此次审查旨在确保必要时能够顺利注资。当被问及政府是否会扩大基金规模时，他说，主管部门将在任何注资发生时评估当时的市场状况，再决定基金规模。他的表态正值投资者对人工智能（AI）前景以及AI投资回报的疑虑日益加深、投资者信心受损之际。随着全球市场波动加剧，以科技股为主的纳斯达克指数下跌，韩国股市也大幅下挫。周日举行的一次紧急会议上，李与韩国银行、金融服务委员会和金融监督_service（FSS）的负责人同意为可能注资股市稳定基金做准备，并审查基金的实际运作方式。FSS和韩国交易所还宣布，将在三个月内加强对非法卖空的监测。该基金汇集券商、银行和其他机构的资金，在市场急剧下跌、需求枯竭时买入股票。主管部门上一次动用股市稳定基金是在2008年全球金融危机期间，共投入5150亿韩元（3.82亿美元）。2020年新冠疫情期间，韩国还设立了一个规模为10.76万亿韩元的独立基金，但该基金一直未动用。李承诺密切留意交易动态，因为市场走势难以预测。当被问及是否会采取进一步措施时，李说：“我们已经制定了应急方案，正在准备在适当时机采取行动。”他说，主管部门将利用这三个月加强打击非法卖空，并监测不公平交易。尽管融资和监管方面的担忧仍在，李预计近期AI投资将继续增长。他说，韩国两大芯片制造商Samsung Electronics和SK hynix已通过长期供应合同获得大量订单，其存储芯片库存正在迅速下降。他还预计，美国中期选举后可能出现的监管变化，对明年AI数据中心建设的影响有限，因为计划开工的大部分美国项目已经取得许可。与此同时，李表示，除非出现意外冲击，韩国经济今年很可能增长3%多一点。当被问及一些投资银行预测经济增长率达到4%或更高时，他说：“从数学上看，我认为4%是可以实现的。”他还说，最终结果将取决于第四季度的增长表现

https://www.myjoyonline.com/gsa-launches.title: GSA launches digital platform to fight Non-Tariff Barriers

https://www.myjoyonline.com/gsa-launches.body: The Ghana Shippers’ Authority (GSA) has developed a digital Non-Tariff Barriers (NTB) Reporting and Resolution Platform in collaboration with the Ministry of Trade, Agribusiness and Industry, with support from Trade Mark Africa to enhance cargo movements from the ports. Speaking at a media engagement, the CEO Prof. Ransford Gyampo said the movement of goods is often impeded by non-tariff barriers which cost traders’ time and money — but most are never reported and never resolved. “With the NTB platform, anyone can report a barrier, from the Web, WhatsApp, social media and a simple USSD Code,” he said. The platform will facilitate the reporting, monitoring and resolution of trade-related barriers. The NTB platform is part of a wider digital transformation drive. The Authority advanced the integration of shipper registration onto the Integrated Customs Management System (ICUMS) to strengthen its shipper database and enhance evidence-based regulatory oversight. Previously, the absence of a comprehensive and reliable database of shippers constrained the Authority’s ability to discharge its regulatory responsibilities and respond to shippers’ needs. Prof. Gyampo said the Authority has expanded its operations to 24 hours in support of Government’s 24-Hour Economy agenda, after preparing and presenting a policy paper to the Presidency outlining its contribution. “The Government of Ghana’s 24-Hour Economy Policy represents a transformative national agenda aimed at repositioning the country as a competitive, export-driven and industrialized economy capable of sustaining continuous economic activity,” he said. Other digital and trade facilitation gains in 2026 included sustained transit corridor monitoring, which contributed to a reduction in checkpoints along Ghana’s transit corridors, particularly on routes serving landlocked Burkina Faso, Mali and Niger. The Authority also successfully hosted the 2026 Annual Borderless Forum with Borderless Alliance, focusing on digital trade facilitation and regional integration. For 2027, accelerating digital transformation and data-driven trade facilitation is one of five strategic priorities — alongside strengthening regulatory oversight, deepening stakeholder engagement, promoting logistics infrastructure, and strengthening institutional capacity

Unlock these with Subscription In a bid to boost connectivity and bilateral ties with Nepal, the Ministry of Railways has launched Ayodhya Cantt-Janakpur Dham weekly express . Prime Minister Narendra Modi and his Nepalese counterpart Balendra Shah virtually flagged off the Saryu-Kamala Express, connecting Ayodhya in Uttar Pradesh to Janakpur in Nepal, from Delhi on Monday (November 23, 2026). The weekly train will establish a crucial rail link between two pilgrimage sites, namely Janakpur Dham and Ayodhya, believed to be the birthplace of Sita and Ram. Further, the initiative is expected to enhance trade and cultural ties between both countries. The train will cover a distance of approximately 604 kilometres in 19 hours, passing through several important towns in Bihar and Uttar Pradesh . The weekly train will commence its journey from Janakpur Dham on Saturday, and from Ayodhya Cantt on Monday. The express train will commence regular service from November 28. The originating train (15596) from India is scheduled to depart from its station at Ayodhya Cantt. at 5:50 p.m every Monday, and reach the final destination at Janakpur at 12:40 p.m. (Nepali time) next day. On its return journey, the train will leave Janakpur Dham at 1.10 pm (Nepali time) every Saturday and reach Ayodhya Cantt at 8.10 am on Sundays. The train is scheduled to halt at 10 stations as part of its itinerary. Here is the list of stations where the train will have stoppages besides its terminal stations. The Saryu-Kamala Express will be operated using modern 17-coach LHB (Linke Hofmann Busch) rakes. The train configuration includes eight air-conditioned coaches, seven sleeper-class coaches, one LSLRD (LHB Second Class, Luggage, Brake, and Disabled-friendly) coach, and one LWLRRM (LHB Power Car/Generator-cum-Luggage-cum-Brake Van) coach. The ticket prices for the Ayodhya Cantt-Janakpur Dham weekly express are yet to be announced on the IRCTC website. Indian citizens going to Nepal don’t need a visa if they have a valid passport. https://x.com/ngmarketlens/status/212559.snippet:
🇺🇸 The US is opening another front in global trade tensions. But could Nigeria actually benefit from it?

The Trump administration has proposed new tariffs targeting 14 trading partners following a Section 301 investigation into industrial overcapacity, according to Reuters.

Among the proposed measures:

• China: An additional 20% tariff on top of existing first-term duties.
• Vietnam: A proposed 20% tariff.
• EU, Japan, South Korea and Taiwan: Existing 15% tariff caps to be respected.
• Malaysia: Existing 19% tariff cap to be respected.

Nigeria is not among the economies highlighted here, but that does not mean Nigeria is insulated from the consequences.

There are four important channels to watch.

1. Could imported goods become cheaper in Nigeria?

If Chinese manufacturers face higher barriers to the US market, some may redirect their products towards Africa and other emerging markets.

For Nigeria, this could mean more competitive prices for machinery, electronics, solar equipment, vehicles and industrial materials.

That could benefit consumers and businesses looking to reduce costs.

But there is another side to this.

An influx of competitively priced imports could put additional pressure on Nigerian manufacturers already struggling with expensive electricity, financing and logistics.

Cheaper imports can ease inflation while simultaneously making domestic industrial development more difficult.

2. Oil revenues and the naira

Escalating trade tensions could weaken global economic growth and reduce demand for crude oil.

For Nigeria, lower oil prices could translate into:

• Reduced export earnings.
• Lower government revenues.
• Weaker dollar inflows.
• Additional pressure on the naira.

And remember, cheaper Chinese products do not necessarily mean cheaper products in Nigerian shops if the naira weakens at the same time.

3. Global capital flows

If higher tariffs contribute to persistent US inflation, the Federal Reserve could keep interest rates higher for longer.

Combined with today’s hotter-than-expected US core PCE inflation, this is something Nigerian investors should be watching closely.

Higher US yields could make emerging-market assets less attractive to international investors, increasing competition for the foreign capital Nigeria needs.

4. A potential opportunity for Nigerian manufacturing

Global trade fragmentation is encouraging companies to reconsider where they manufacture, source materials and distribute their products.

Nigeria has a large domestic market, access to regional markets through AfCFTA, natural resources and expanding industrial capacity.

Could Nigeria attract some of the investment looking for alternative production locations?

Potentially, yes.

But investors will also compare electricity costs, infrastructure, regulatory predictability, financing conditions and logistics with competing destinations.

Market size alone will not be enough.

What I find particularly interesting here is the potential contradiction.

Nigeria could benefit from cheaper imported equipment while facing greater competition from imported finished goods.

The first could strengthen domestic production. The second could undermine it.

The difference will depend largely on how effectively Nigeria turns affordable industrial inputs into competitive local manufacturing.

Global trade tensions create risks, but they also redistribute economic opportunities.

For Nigeria, the bigger question is whether we can capture those opportunities as a producer, rather than simply becoming another destination for surplus global production.

https://x.com/ngmarketlens/status/212559.snippet_zh:
🇺🇸 美国正在全球贸易紧张局势中开辟另一条战线。但尼日利亚真的能从中受益吗？

据路透社报道，特朗普政府在依据《贸易法》第301条对工业产能过剩展开调查后，提议对14个贸易伙伴加征新关税。

拟议措施包括：

• 中国：在现有首任期关税的基础上再加征20%关税。
• 越南：拟加征20%关税。
• 欧盟、日本、韩国和中国台湾：须遵守现行15%的关税上限。
• 马来西亚：须遵守现行19%的关税上限。

尼日利亚不在此次重点列出的经济体之列，但这并不意味着尼日利亚可以免受其影响。

有四条重要渠道值得关注。

1. 进口商品在尼日利亚会不会变得更便宜？

如果中国制造商进入美国市场面临更高壁垒，其中一些企业可能会将产品转向非洲及其他新兴市场。

对尼日利亚而言，这意味着机械、电子产品、太阳能设备、车辆和工业材料的价格可能更具竞争力。

这可能让希望降低成本的消费者和企业受益。

但事情还有另一面。

大量具有价格竞争力的进口商品涌入，可能进一步挤压尼日利亚制造商，而他们已经在高企的电费、融资成本和物流成本下艰难经营。

更便宜的进口商品可以缓解通胀，同时也会使本土工业发展更加困难。

2. 石油收入与奈拉

贸易紧张局势升级可能削弱全球经济增长，并降低原油需求。

对尼日利亚而言，油价下跌可能意味着：

• 出口收入减少。
• 政府收入下降。
• 美元流入减少。
• 奈拉承受更大压力。

此外还要记住，如果奈拉同时贬值，中国商品价格下降未必意味着尼日利亚商店里的商品也会变得更便宜。

3. 全球资本流动

如果更高关税助推美国通胀持续，美联储可能会更长时间维持较高利率。

结合目前高于预期的美国核心PCE通胀，这是尼日利亚投资者应当密切关注的因素。

美国收益率上升可能降低新兴市场资产对国际投资者的吸引力，从而加剧对尼日利亚所需外国资本的竞争。

4. 尼日利亚制造业的潜在机遇

全球贸易碎片化正促使企业重新考虑生产地点、原材料采购地和产品分销地。

尼日利亚拥有庞大的国内市场，可通过AfCFTA进入区域市场，并拥有自然资源和不断扩大的工业产能。

尼日利亚能否吸引部分寻求替代生产地点的投资？

有可能。

但投资者也会将当地的电力成本、基础设施、监管可预测性、融资条件和物流成本与其他目的地进行比较。

仅凭市场规模并不足够。

我觉得这里尤其值得关注的是一种潜在矛盾。

尼日利亚既可能从更便宜的进口设备中受益，又将面临进口制成品带来的更大竞争。

前者可以增强国内生产，后者则可能削弱国内生产。

最终结果在很大程度上取决于尼日利亚能否高效地将价格可负担的工业投入品转化为具有竞争力的本地制造业。

全球贸易紧张局势会带来风险，但也会重新分配经济机遇。

对尼日利亚而言，更大的问题在于，我们能否以生产国的身份把握这些机遇，而不是仅仅成为全球过剩产能的另一个销售目的地。

https://x.com/onibudoireke/status/212556.snippet:
Five years after the Federal Executive Council signed off on nearly $3 billion to fix Nigeria’s state-owned refineries, sustained commercial petrol production from those plants remains out of reach. Port Harcourt briefly restarted in late 2024 before shutting down months later. Warri reopened shortly afterward and went offline again over operational and safety concerns. Today, Nigerians are right back where they started, asking what public value was delivered for one of the largest rehabilitation commitments in our history.

On paper, the 2021 approvals alone were staggering. The federal government approved $1.5 billion for the Port Harcourt refinery contract awarded to Maire Tecnimont, alongside $897.68 million for Warri and $586.90 million for Kaduna, initially announced for Saipem with Daewoo E&C later brought in on quick-fix packages. Together, those approvals came to $2.985 billion. At today’s official CBN rate of roughly ₦1,394 to the dollar, that commitment equals about ₦4.16 trillion in present-day terms, sitting atop wider Turnaround Maintenance spending between 2010 and 2023 that legislative inquiries and analysts have estimated in the tens of billions of dollars.

To be fair to the record, approved contract ceilings are not the same thing as verified cash disbursements. Nor was the naira trading at today’s rate in 2021. Yet that gap in public knowledge is precisely the problem. Years down the line, taxpayers still do not have a consolidated, line-by-line public account showing how much was actually released, what engineering milestones were independently certified, and why the plants could not stay on stream. Energy analysts have long pointed out that sums of this magnitude approach what it takes to finance modern, purpose-built refining capacity from the ground up.

That history makes an older, unresolved industry story from the Buhari administration worth revisiting. According to unconfirmed industry accounts, Chinese energy giant Sinopec approached NNPC during that period with an offer to repair, restore, and help run the Warri and Port Harcourt refineries, before decision-makers opted for another route. There is no public document proving that a formal offer landed on NNPC’s desk, and NNPC Ltd can easily put the matter to rest by stating whether one was ever received and why it did or did not advance.

The question matters because credentials in heavy industry matter. Sinopec is the world’s largest refiner by capacity, processing roughly 5 million barrels of crude a day. That is more than eleven times the 445,000 barrels per day combined nameplate capacity of Port Harcourt, Warri, and Kaduna. Through Sinopec Engineering Group, it has executed complex refinery builds and revamps from Saudi Arabia’s Yasref complex to Algeria’s Hassi Messaoud and Arzew projects. In global refining, Sinopec commands the sort of engineering reputation that Nigerians associate with Julius Berger in major road and civil infrastructure.

Which brings us to April 30, 2026. In Jiaxing City, China, NNPC Ltd signed a fresh Memorandum of Understanding for a potential Technical Equity Partnership covering Port Harcourt and Warri. Only this time, the prospective partners were not a global refining major like Sinopec, but two private Chinese firms: Sanjiang Chemical Company Limited and Xinganchen (Fuzhou) Industrial Park Operation and Management Co. Ltd.

Almost immediately, voices in Nigeria’s organised private sector raised eyebrows. Critics, including former Organised Private Sector of Nigeria (OPSN) president Dele Oye, publicly questioned whether companies profiled mainly around chemical manufacturing and industrial park real estate possess a verifiable track record of rehabilitating and operating complex crude oil refineries.

NNPC Ltd has stressed that the April MoU is only a preliminary framework. If that is the case, there is still room to get this right before binding equity or operating contracts are signed.

Before Nigeria enters another chapter of refinery promises, four things ought to happen in full view of the public:

First, NNPC Ltd should publish a comprehensive financial and technical audit of all refinery rehabilitation contracts since 2010, detailing what was approved, what was actually paid out, and what work was independently certified.

Second, NNPC Ltd and the project contractors should give Nigerians a clear status report on contractual deliverables completed and any obligations still outstanding on the 2021 awards.

Third, NNPC Ltd should clarify once and for all whether Sinopec or other tier-one international refiners ever submitted proposals for our refineries, and how those proposals were assessed.

Fourth, the technical and financial due diligence on Sanjiang and Xinganchen should be made public alongside clear, competitive selection benchmarks before any binding deal is sealed.

Nigeria’s refining crisis has never been caused by a lack of crude, market demand, or capable global engineers. It stems from opaque procurement and a habit of moving on to the next announcement without accounting for the last one. Public assets belong to the Nigerian people, and asking for audited facts is the bare minimum of democratic accountability.

Together, those approvals came to $2.985 billion. At today’s official CBN rate of roughly ₦1,394 to the dollar, that commitment equals about ₦4.16 trillion in present-day terms, sitting atop wider Turnaround Maintenance spending between 2010 and 2023 that legislative inquiries and analysts have estimated in the tens of billions of dollars.

To be fair to the record, approved contract ceilings are not the same thing as verified cash disbursements. Nor was the naira trading at today’s rate in 2021. Yet that gap in public knowledge is precisely the problem. Years down the line, taxpayers still do not have a consolidated, line-by-line public account showing how much was actually released, what engineering milestones were independently certified, and why the plants could not stay on stream. Energy analysts have long pointed out that sums of this magnitude approach what it takes to finance modern, purpose-built refining capacity from the ground up.

That history makes an older, unresolved industry story from the Buhari administration worth revisiting. According to unconfirmed industry accounts, Chinese energy giant Sinopec approached NNPC during that period with an offer to repair, restore, and help run the Warri and Port Harcourt refineries, before decision-makers opted for another route. There is no public document proving that a formal offer landed on NNPC’s desk, and NNPC Ltd can easily put the matter to rest by stating whether one was ever received and why it did or did not advance.

The question matters because credentials in heavy industry matter. Sinopec is the world’s largest refiner by capacity, processing roughly 5 million barrels of crude a day. That is more than eleven times the 445,000 barrels per day combined nameplate capacity of Port Harcourt, Warri, and Kaduna. Through Sinopec Engineering Group, it has executed complex refinery builds and revamps from Saudi Arabia’s Yasref complex to Algeria’s Hassi Messaoud and Arzew projects. In global refining, Sinopec commands the sort of engineering reputation that Nigerians associate with Julius Berger in major road and civil infrastructure.

Which brings us to April 30, 2026. In Jiaxing City, China, NNPC Ltd signed a fresh Memorandum of Understanding for a potential Technical Equity Partnership covering Port Harcourt and Warri. Only this time, the prospective partners were not a global refining major like Sinopec, but two private Chinese firms: Sanjiang Chemical Company Limited and Xinganchen (Fuzhou) Industrial Park Operation and Management Co. Ltd.

Almost immediately, voices in Nigeria’s organised private sector raised eyebrows. Critics, including former Organised Private Sector of Nigeria (OPSN) president Dele Oye, publicly questioned whether companies profiled mainly around chemical manufacturing and industrial park real estate possess a verifiable track record of rehabilitating and operating complex crude oil refineries.

NNPC Ltd has stressed that the April MoU is only a preliminary framework. If that is the case, there is still room to get this right before binding equity or operating contracts are signed.

Before Nigeria enters another chapter of refinery promises, four things ought to happen in full view of the public:

First, NNPC Ltd should publish a comprehensive financial and technical audit of all refinery rehabilitation contracts since 2010, detailing what was approved, what was actually paid out, and what work was independently certified.

Second, NNPC Ltd and the project contractors should give Nigerians a clear status report on contractual deliverables completed and any obligations still outstanding on the 2021 awards.

Third, NNPC Ltd should clarify once and for all whether Sinopec or other tier-one international refiners ever submitted proposals for our refineries, and how those proposals were assessed.

Fourth, the technical and financial due diligence on Sanjiang and Xinganchen should be made public alongside clear, competitive selection benchmarks before any binding deal is sealed.

Nigeria’s refining crisis has never been caused by a lack of crude, market demand, or capable global engineers. It stems from opaque procurement and a habit of moving on to the next announcement without accounting for the last one. Public assets belong to the Nigerian people, and asking for audited facts is the bare minimum of democratic accountability.
https://x.com/onibudoireke/status/212556.title_zh: 联邦执行委员会批准近30亿美元用于修复尼日利亚国有炼油厂五年后，持续的商业
https://x.com/onibudoireke/status/212556.snippet_zh:
联邦执行委员会批准近30亿美元用于修缮尼日利亚国有炼油厂已过去五年，这些炼油厂持续实现商业化汽油生产仍遥不可及。哈特科特港炼油厂在2024年底短暂复产，数月后又停产。瓦里炼油厂不久后重新开工，却因运营和安全方面的疑虑再次停摆。如今，尼日利亚人又回到了原点，追问我国历史上最大规模的修缮承诺之一，究竟交付了多少公共价值。

仅从账面看，2021年的批准金额就十分惊人。联邦政府批准了15亿美元用于哈特科特港炼油厂合同，该合同授予Maire Tecnimont；同时批准瓦里炼油厂8.9768亿美元、卡杜纳炼油厂5.869亿美元，后者最初宣布授予Saipem，后来引入大宇E&C承接快速修复项目。这些批准金额合计达29.85亿美元。按尼日利亚中央银行目前约1,394奈拉兑1美元的官方汇率计算，这笔承诺按今天的水平约合4.16万亿奈拉，而这一切还叠加在2010年至2023年间更大规模的周转维护支出之上——立法调查和分析人士估计这部分支出达数百亿美元。

公平地说，已批准的合同上限并不等于经核实的现金拨付。2021年时奈拉的汇率也不是今天的水平。然而，正是在公共认知上的这一落差构成了问题。时至今日，纳税人仍无法获得一份整合的、逐项列明的公开账目，说明实际拨付了多少资金、哪些工程节点获得了独立认证，以及这些炼油厂为何无法持续运行。能源分析人士早就指出，这一量级的资金已接近从头建设现代化专用炼油能力所需的投入。

这段历史让布赫里政府时期一桩悬而未决、值得重提的行业旧事重新引人关注。据未经证实的行业说法，中国能源巨头中国石化当时曾接触尼日利亚国家石油公司，提出修复、翻新并协助运营瓦里和哈特科特港两座炼油厂，之后决策者选择了另一条路。没有公开文件能证明正式报价曾送达尼日利亚国家石油公司的案头，而尼日利亚国家石油公司有限公司只需说明是否曾收到过此类报价、为何推进或不推进，便可轻易了结此事。

之所以重要，是因为重工业领域的资质至关重要。中国石化是全球按产能计最大的炼油企业，每日加工约500万桶原油。这比哈特科特港、瓦里和卡杜纳三厂合计44.5万桶/日的铭牌产能高出十一倍以上。通过中国石化工程集团，中国石化已完成从沙特Yasref综合体到阿尔及利亚Hassi Messaoud和Arzew项目等复杂炼油新建与改造工程。在全球炼油领域，中国石化拥有尼日利亚人常与朱利叶斯·伯杰在大型道路和土木基础设施上相提并论的那种工程声誉。

这就引出了2026年4月30日。在中国嘉兴市，尼日利亚国家石油公司有限公司签署了一份新的谅解备忘录，涉及哈特科特港和瓦里炼油厂的潜在技术股权伙伴关系。只是这一次，潜在伙伴并非中国石化这样的全球炼油巨头，而是两家中国民营企业：浙江三江化工股份有限公司和兴安晨（福州）工业园运营管理有限公司。

几乎是立刻，尼日利亚有组织的私营部门就提出了质疑。批评者包括尼日利亚有组织私营部门前主席Dele Oye，他们公开质疑：主要业务集中于化工制造和工业园地产的公司，是否具备修缮并运营复杂原油炼油厂的可核实业绩记录。

尼日利亚国家石油公司有限公司强调，4月的谅解备忘录只是一个初步框架。如果确实如此，那么在签署具有约束力的股权或运营合同之前，仍有空间把事情做对。

在尼日利亚开启又一轮炼油厂承诺之前，有四件事应当在公众注视下完成：

第一，尼日利亚国家石油公司有限公司应公布一份涵盖2010年以来所有炼油厂修缮合同的综合性财务与技术审计报告，详细说明批准了什么、实际支付了多少、哪些工程获得了独立认证。

第二，尼日利亚国家石油公司有限公司和项目承包商应向尼日利亚人提交一份清晰的状态报告，说明2021年批准项目中已完成的合同交付内容以及仍未履行的义务。

第三，尼日利亚国家石油公司有限公司应彻底澄清，中国石化或其他一流国际炼油企业是否曾就我国炼油厂提交过方案，以及这些方案是如何评估的。

第四，在敲定任何具有约束力的交易之前，应公开对浙江三江和兴安晨的技术与财务尽职调查，并同时公布明确、具竞争性的遴选基准。

尼日利亚的炼油危机从来不是由原油短缺、市场需求不足或缺乏称职的全球工程师造成的。它根源在不透明的采购，以及在未对上一次公告作出交代的情况下就转向下一次公告的惯性与做法。公共资产属于尼日利亚人民，索取经审计的事实不过是民主问责的最低要求。

The Pwalugu Tomato Factory, originally started by Dr. Kwame Nkrumah, is set to open again after many years.

Peppers
Garden eggs
Beans

https://x.com/instablog9ja/status/212554.snippet:
Nigeria Is Not A Dumping Ground — Senator Ben Murray-Bruce Calls For Stricter Regulations To Protect Nigerian Consumers

Senator Ben Murray-Bruce has called on the Federal Government to introduce stricter regulations to protect Nigerian consumers from companies selling products without proper warranties, spare parts and after-sales services.

He raised concerns over foreign car brands, particularly Chinese manufacturers, opening showrooms in major cities such as Lagos and Abuja, only to shut down and leave customers stranded without access to repairs or replacement parts.

Sharing his personal experience, Murray-Bruce said he invested in a solar power system for his home, but the company that installed it went bankrupt and left Nigeria within a year, rendering his investment useless because there was no one to service it.

He described the situation as exploitation rather than trade, insisting that companies operating in Nigeria must demonstrate their capacity to provide long-term support for the products they sell.

He urged the Minister of Industry, Trade and Investment, Dr Jumoke Oduwole, and the Minister of State for Industry, Senator John Owan Enoh, to establish stricter entry requirements for companies seeking to operate in the Nigerian market.

He also called on the National Automotive Design and Development Council, the Standards Organisation of Nigeria and the Federal Competition and Consumer Protection Commission to ensure that dealerships are properly licensed, substandard products are kept out of the country and consumers are protected.

On solar power systems and inverters, Murray-Bruce urged the Minister of Power, Joseph Tegbe, to insist that only certified installers with long-term service commitments operate in the sector.

Among his proposed measures, he suggested that companies should provide financial bonds, guarantee spare parts and after-sales services for a minimum number of years, and establish local service centres before selling their products.

He further proposed that dealerships that shut down within five years of operating should be held accountable, with their directors pursued and affected customers compensated.

Concluding his message, he stressed that Nigeria’s market of more than 200 million people should not be treated as a dumping ground for products and companies that cannot provide lasting support to consumers.

https://x.com/instablog9ja/status/212554.snippet_zh:
尼日利亚不是倾销地——参议员本·默里-布鲁斯呼吁加强监管，保护尼日利亚消费者
参议员本·默里-布鲁斯呼吁联邦政府出台更严格的监管措施，防止向消费者销售产品却不提供适当保修、备件和售后服务的公司损害消费者利益。
他对外来汽车品牌，尤其是中国制造商在拉各斯、阿布贾等主要城市开设展厅，随后关闭门店并让客户陷入困境、无法获得维修或更换零部件服务的情况表示担忧。
默里-布鲁斯分享了自己的亲身经历：他曾为家中投资安装太阳能供电系统，但负责安装的公司在一年内破产并离开尼日利亚，使其投资变得毫无用处，因为已无人能够提供维护服务。
他将这种局面描述为剥削而非贸易，坚持在尼日利亚经营的公司必须证明其有能力为所售产品提供长期支持。
他敦促工业、贸易与投资部长朱莫克·奥杜沃莱博士，以及工业部国务参议员约翰·奥万·埃诺赫，为寻求进入尼日利亚市场的公司制定更严格的准入要求。
他还呼吁尼日利亚汽车设计与开发委员会、尼日利亚标准组织和联邦竞争与消费者保护委员会，确保经销商取得适当许可、不合格产品被阻挡在国门外，并保护消费者权益。
谈及太阳能供电系统和逆变器，默里-布鲁斯敦促电力部长约瑟夫·特格贝坚持要求该行业仅由承诺提供长期服务的认证安装商经营。
在提出的措施中，他建议公司在销售产品之前缴纳财务保证金、保证在一定最低年限内提供备件和售后服务，并设立本地服务中心。
他进一步建议，对开业五年内关停的经销商追究责任，追究其董事责任，并赔偿受影响的消费者。
他在结束发言时强调，拥有超过2亿人口的市场尼日利亚，不应成为无法为消费者提供持久支持的产品和公司的倾销地。

https://x.com/1thinkingafrica/status/212.title: For over a century, the world has played the same trick on Africa: dig up the rock, ship it out cheap - and sell back the finished product a
https://x.com/1thinkingafrica/status/212.snippet:
For over a century, the world has played the same trick on Africa: dig up the rock, ship it out cheap - and sell back the finished product at ten times the price. With just weeks to go before Zimbabwe's full ban on lithium concentrate exports hits on 1 January 2027, Harare is refusing to blink.

In mid-November, mining companies lobbied for a delay, warning that enforcing the deadline could leave 1.4-million tonnes of unprocessed concentrate sitting in stockpiles. Zim's answer was blunt - instead of backing down, Finance Minister Mthuli Ncube tightened the 10% export tax rules on raw concentrate and mandated local sourcing, while keeping processed lithium sulphate exports completely tax free.

The standoff rests on real proof of concept. At the Arcadia mine outside Harare, a $400-million processing plant run by Prospect Lithium Zimbabwe - a subsidiary of China's Zhejiang Huayou Cobalt - began Africa's first commercial exports of lithium sulphate in April 2026. Between April and September alone, Zimbabwe shipped 33,807 tonnes of the battery-grade precursor (worth roughly $190 million) as the 50,000-tonne facility ramps up.

What started with Zimbabwe banning raw lithium ore exports back in 2022 - followed by a June 2025 notice to end concentrate exports and an abrupt February 2026 crackdown on illegal shipments - has forced miners to build on African soil. Rival Chinese giants Sinomine and Sichuan Yahua are now racing to finish their own sulphate plants at Bikita and Kamativi, with industry forecasts projecting Zimbabwe's output to surge to 208,000 tonnes in 2027.

Zim is not acting alone. Since 2023, roughly 14 African governments - including Burkina Faso, DRC, Gabon, Ghana, Kenya, Malawi, Namibia and Tanzania - have moved to restrict raw ore exports, suspend or overhaul mining licences, or mandate domestic refining.

But the hard sovereignty test still lies ahead. Foreign firms still own the plants, and lithium sulphate is only the middle rung of the battery supply chain. True economic liberation means using leverage like Harare's January deadline to capture local skills, power infrastructure and eventually African-owned refining all the way to finished batteries.

Is holding the line on raw export bans the turning point for African industrialisation - or does the continent need to push even harder for local ownership?

https://x.com/1thinkingafrica/status/212.title_zh: 一个多世纪以来，世界对非洲始终使用同一套把戏：低价挖出矿石并运走，再把制成品高价卖回非洲
https://x.com/1thinkingafrica/status/212.snippet_zh: 一个多世纪以来，世界一直对非洲施展同一套把戏：挖出矿石，低价运走，再以十倍的价钱卖回成品。距离津巴布韦全面禁止锂精矿出口的规定于2027年1月1日生效只剩数周，哈拉雷却拒绝退让。  11月中旬，矿业公司游说政府推迟实施，警告称若按期执行，可能导致140万吨未加工精矿堆存在库存中。津巴布韦的回应十分强硬。财政部长姆图利·恩库布不但没有退缩，反而收紧了针对原矿精矿的10%出口税规定， mandate 强制实行本地采购，同时对已加工硫酸锂的出口继续完全免税。  这场对峙有真实的概念验证作为支撑。在哈拉雷郊外的Arcadia矿，由中国浙江华友钴业子公司Prospect Lithium Zimbabwe运营的一座价值4亿美元加工厂，于2026年4月开始非洲首次商业出口硫酸锂。随着这座5万吨产能设施逐步满产，仅4月至9月间，津巴布韦便出口了33,807吨电池级硫酸锂前驱体，价值约1.9亿美元。  津巴布韦从2022年禁止原矿锂出口开始，随后在2025年6月发布终止精矿出口的通知，并于2026年2月突然严厉打击非法运输，迫使矿业企业在非洲本土建设工厂。中国竞争对手Sinomine和Sichuan Yahua目前正竞相完成各自位于Bikita和Kamativi的硫酸锂工厂。行业预测显示，津巴布韦的产量到2027年将激增至208,000吨。  津巴布韦并非独自行动。自2023年以来，包括Burkina Faso、DRC、Gabon、Ghana、Kenya、Malawi、Namibia和Tanzania在内的约14个非洲政府，已采取限制原矿出口、暂停或整顿采矿许可证，或强制要求国内精炼等措施。  但真正考验主权的时刻仍在前方。外国企业目前仍拥有这些工厂，而硫酸锂不过是电池供应链的中间一环。真正的经济解放，是利用哈拉雷设定的一月最后期限这一筹码，将本地技能、电力基础设施，乃至最终由非洲企业拥有的精炼产能和成品电池生产环节掌握在自己手中。  坚持执行原矿出口禁令，会成为非洲工业化的转折点吗？还是说，这片大陆需要进一步推动本地所有权？

https://x.com/seriesaglobal/status/21248.title: Ghana Gas says it replaced 52 Chinese expatriate engineers with Ghanaians and now saves $3.
https://x.com/seriesaglobal/status/21248.snippet:
Ghana Gas says it replaced 52 Chinese expatriate engineers with Ghanaians and now saves $3.5M a month. Localisation is the story, and the figure is the CEO's claim.

Ghana Gas's CEO, Dr Ben Asante, told gas conference participants touring the Atuabo plant in the Western Region that the company had phased out 52 Chinese expatriates who ran its technical operations. It trained Ghanaian engineers to take their place, and the plant is now run by about 50 Ghanaians. Asante said the company had been paying the expatriates about $3.5M a month and that there had been no incidents at the plant. Atuabo supplies gas to the Aboadze thermal plant, a major part of the country's power supply.

This is a bigger deal than a payroll change. Gas processing is a safety-critical industry, and the usual argument for foreign operators is that local teams can't be trusted with it. Asante said the idea drew scepticism at first, partly because of an earlier accident at a state power plant. Handing the plant to local engineers and reporting no incidents is the kind of result that can change how African countries approach local content, which usually means quotas and not full takeover.

The $3.5M figure needs a closer look. Divided across 52 people, that's about $67,000 per person per month (our arithmetic), which is too high for salaries alone. It likely covers the contractor's fees and overheads too. Later versions of the claim moved around. In January 2023 the CEO said $207M had been saved since March 2017, at about $3M a month, and in November 2024 he said over $250M.

https://x.com/seriesaglobal/status/21248.title_zh: Ghana Gas表示，已用加纳人取代52名中国外籍工程师，如今每年节省3亿美元。
https://x.com/seriesaglobal/status/21248.snippet_zh:
Ghana Gas表示，已用加纳人取代52名中国外籍工程师，如今每月节省350万美元。本地化是这项措施的核心，而这一数字是首席执行官的说法。

Ghana Gas首席执行官Ben Asante博士在参观西部地区Atuabo工厂的天然气会议与会者面前表示，公司已逐步淘汰负责其技术运营的52名中国外籍人员。公司培训了加纳工程师接替他们的工作，如今工厂约有50名加纳人负责运营。Asante说，公司此前每月向这些外籍人员支付约350万美元，而且工厂没有发生过任何事故。Atuabo工厂向Aboadze热电站供应天然气，后者是加纳电力供应的重要组成部分。

这比单纯调整工资名单意义重大。天然气加工属于安全攸关行业，支持外国运营商的常见论点是，本地团队无法胜任这项工作。Asante表示，这一想法起初遭到质疑，部分原因是此前一座国营发电厂发生过事故。将工厂交给本地工程师运营并报告称没有事故，是能够改变非洲国家看待本地化方式的一类成果；本地化通常意味着设定外籍人员比例，而不是完全由本地人员接管。

350万美元这一数字需要进一步审视。按52人分摊，人均每月约67,000美元（我们的计算结果），仅凭工资收入而言太高了。这一数字很可能还涵盖承包商费用和间接开支。后来关于这一说法出现了不同版本。2023年1月，首席执行官表示，自2017年3月以来已节省2.07亿美元，平均每月约300万美元；2024年11月，他又表示节省金额超过2.5亿美元。

Ghana Gas表示，已用加纳人取代52名中国外籍工程师，如今每月节省350万美元。本地化是这项措施的核心，而这一数字是首席执行官的说法。

Ghana Gas首席执行官Ben Asante博士在参观西部地区Atuabo工厂的天然气会议与会者面前表示，公司已逐步淘汰负责其技术运营的52名中国外籍人员。公司培训了加纳工程师接替他们的工作，如今工厂约有50名加纳人负责运营。Asante说，公司此前每月向这些外籍人员支付约350万美元，而且工厂没有发生过任何事故。Atuabo工厂向Aboadze热电站供应天然气，后者是加纳电力供应的重要组成部分。

这比单纯调整工资名单意义重大。天然气加工属于安全攸关行业，支持外国运营商的常见论点是，本地团队无法胜任这项工作。Asante表示，这一想法起初遭到质疑，部分原因是此前一座国营发电厂发生过事故。将工厂交给本地工程师运营并报告称没有事故，是能够改变非洲国家看待本地化方式的一类成果；本地化通常意味着设定外籍人员比例，而不是完全由本地人员接管。

350万美元这一数字需要进一步审视。按52人分摊，人均每月约67,000美元（我们的计算结果），仅凭工资收入而言太高了。这一数字很可能还涵盖承包商费用和间接开支。后来关于这一说法出现了不同版本。2023年1月，首席执行官表示，自2017年3月以来已节省2.07亿美元，平均每月约300万美元；2024年11月，他又表示节省金额超过2.5亿美元。
